speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a skin condition of concern; to begin our evaluation, how long have you noticed the lesion, and has its appearance or size changed recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the patient's age, heavy smoking history, and the non-healing nature of the lesions on the penis and finger, I am concerned about squamous cell carcinoma. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, HbA1c, and Lipid Panel. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy of penile and digital lesions. Do you have any history of genital warts or chronic sun exposure to your hands?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of non-healing, crusty lesions on your penile shaft and finger, combined with your age and significant smoking history, is highly suggestive of Squamous Cell Carcinoma. I have already requested necessary blood work and dermoscopic images to confirm this. Given the urgency of your concern and the high probability of malignancy, do you have any history of prior skin cancer or immunosuppression?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No known malignancies or hereditary diseases in the family. Previous treatments for syphilis and eczema. Social history: Lives with his 4th wife, smokes 2 packs of cigarettes per day for the last 30 years, has recently immigrated from Africa.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the penile shaft and digit. The clinical presentation of non-healing, crusty lesions in a heavy smoker, combined with the failure of treatments for syphilis and eczema, is highly specific for this malignancy.
